I pulled live telemetry from the dedicated farm (pool-id: dp-84b). Observations:
- Sustained KV-cache pressure; average KV-cache eviction increased 12x in the last 30m.
- Some model variants serving CW are queued behind large-batch jobs from a different tenant; autoscaler failed to spin new nodes because of a transient driver failure in that AZ.
- Error class: upstream GPU OOM + transient RPC timeouts to the worker (5xx).

Immediate mitigation I’m running now:
1) Drain the non-essential batch queue (ongoing).
2) Force-roll a small subset of the pool to the alternate kernel set (will take ~7min to reprovision).
3) Apply a short-lived routing rule to divert new ClearWire requests to a lower-cost 8-bit quantized variant that is verified compatible for checkout flows.

I’ll post logs and the mitigation runbook snippet in 10 min.

—Jonas
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Team and Tom — summary and next steps below. I’m copying David for final sign-off on credits and exec communication.

Root cause (preliminary):
- Dedicated pool dp-84b experienced an autoscaler driver failure in us-west-2 leading to delayed node reprovision. Large multi-tenant batch jobs (unrelated customer) consumed KV-cache and forced eviction. Combined, this caused RPC timeouts and GPU OOMs for some worker processes running the standard ClearWire variant.

Actions taken:
- Drained non-essential batch jobs (complete).
- Forced routing to a validated 8-bit quantized variant for ClearWire (complete).
- Reprovisioned 6 nodes with alternate kernel set (complete).
- Added short-term safety throttle that caps batch sizes across the pool.

Durable fixes proposed:
1) Pool-level isolation: carve a soft quota for reserved-tenancy pools to prevent noisy-burst batch jobs from using cache headroom (engineering effort: 4 dev-weeks).
2) Autoscaler hardening: better driver failover and faster node reprovision paths (engineering effort: 3 dev-weeks).
3) Billing/credit policy: offer a one-time credit for impacted window + apply a SLA review that guarantees credit thresholds for reserved capacity outages.

Customer ask: ClearWire wants confirmation whether incident time (2026-11-18 08:50–10:05 PST) will be credited and a short technical summary we can share with their exec sponsor. Proposed commercial response: 20% credit on billed reserved capacity for the impacted day and a joint postmortem within 7 business days.

Proposal for exec note (David): I recommend approving the 20% credit and committing to the two engineering items as a priority in Q1 roadmap. We’ll include a short customer-facing note explaining the root cause and remediation timeline.

Next steps / ownership:
- David: sign-off on credit and approve customer-facing note (due EOD tomorrow).
- Jonas: produce final RCA and list of telemetry artifacts for postmortem (due in 3 business days).
- Vanessa: schedule executive summary call with ClearWire and send the commercial note once credit approved (target: within 48 hours).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
